value.change_explanation: The §152(c)(1) rule now observes the literal shared-home interval and recomputes the statutory more-than-one-half condition with inclusive calendar-day arithmetic. When both dates are available, that primitive observation resolves the residence condition even if an older derived boolean conflicts; otherwise an explicitly GIVEN residence intermediate remains usable. In the supplied counterexample, the 2019 overlap is 34 of 365 days, so the residence condition is false and the qualifying-child predicate is definitively false without requiring irrelevant age or joint-return reads. The existing direct GIVEN qualifying-child entry point and other acquired behavior are retained. The other three focused heads are genuinely new acquisitions limited to their exact leaf conditions; §2(a)(1)(A) does not purport to establish the complete surviving-spouse definition. No case-specific names, years, outcomes, native labels, or reference values are embedded.

refinement_contracts.description: If both supported interval dates are present, compute inclusive overlap within the query year and test whether twice that overlap exceeds the number of days in the year. This primitive-date result takes precedence over a conflicting derived residence boolean. If a complete interval is unavailable, an expressly GIVEN scoped residence intermediate remains admissible; otherwise the helper reports the missing observation.

unit_updates.property: whether the identified individual is the taxpayer's qualifying child
unit_updates.quote:
The term "qualifying child" means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, an individual-

        (A) who bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in paragraph (2),

        (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

        (C) who meets the age requirements of paragraph (3), and

        (E) who has not filed a joint return (other than only for a claim of refund) with the individual's spouse for the taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins.
